requirements.requirement: Restore the invoices named in restore-request.txt into live/ with archive-identical bytes and file modes.
requirements.summary: The request names INV-100.txt and INV-101.txt. Both were restored under live/invoices with mode 0644, and their SHA-256 digests exactly match the corresponding archive members, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the current contents of the newer live customer register.
requirements.summary: live/customers.csv retained its original 52-byte contents and SHA-256 digest before restoration, after restoration, and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Do not restore unrelated archived files.
requirements.summary: The archive contained customers.csv and old-notes.txt in addition to the requested invoices. The final live tree contained only the preserved customer register and requested invoices, while live/old-notes.txt was explicitly confirmed absent before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on CentOS 5.11 with kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 before and after the work and restart. Restoration used the platform's available tar utility, with no package or platform replacement evidenced.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are directly satisfied. The mandatory node1 restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, SSH recovered, storage was writable, and the restored and preserved data remained correct. The lifecycle boot observations independently agree. The only hygiene issue is a small leftover restart log in /tmp.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe was unsupported on this pre-systemd platform, although post-restart SSH health was directly verified.

The lifecycle package-health probe invoked an unsupported yum command both before and after execution, so it cannot independently establish package consistency; however, no package-changing executor command is present.
The trace cannot prove whether the initial failed tar attempt made any transient filesystem change, but its errors and the subsequent absence of live/invoices indicate no lasting mutation.
Requirement preserve-customer-register cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Required mutations were limited to creating live/invoices, extracting the two requested files, and performing the mandatory restart. The failed extraction and unprivileged mkdir attempts do not show successful state changes. One executor-created restart log remained at /tmp/benchmark-node-restart.log after completion; it was created by the restart command and not cleaned up, constituting minor temporary-file residue. No package, OS, kernel, service-conflict, or exposure changes are evidenced.
